# soccer-duel-wallclock-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-realtime/1.0`) |

## Task
Robot soccer 2 v 2 under the RoboCup Humanoid Soccer League rules: four simulated Booster T1 humanoids (lower bodies on the released walking policy, held to the real robot's joint limits) and one ball on a boarded 10 x 7 m pitch with two goals, two halves of 5 minutes of game time, a penalty shoot-out when level; each robot takes a walk velocity command, stand or a swing-leg kick, and you see the game only through your robots' head cameras; in the `match` format you command both robots of team A against a scripted team, in the `duel` format another player commands team B, in the `team` format each robot has its own player and teammates talk only through the team channel, in the `team_match` format each robot of team A has its own player against the scripted team; `match_overhead` and `duel_overhead` are match and duel seen through fixed overhead cameras instead of the head cameras; format `duel` (seats A, B),
action level `low`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/soccer/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions) and the first player (`FIRST_PLAYER`; play both orders).
Official matches use the sport's hidden seed set (seeds per format x level: duel: 20, duel_overhead: 20, match/L2: 20, match/L3: 20, match_overhead/L2: 20, match_overhead/L3: 20; sha256 `4f8136d04da2743d4c5ddeea407f2903f8aa0004c265c6685ae0a5be39020899`; `sports/soccer/seed_commitments.json`): the runner gives the sim service one seed of the match's cell and its salt (`RCB_SEED_SALT`), the players never see them, no record shows them (seed -1), and the verifier counts a match as official only when its commitment is in the registered cell (`hidden_seed`, `hidden_seed_index`).
Continuous score `goal_difference` (larger is better; `<seat>_continuous_score`, and `continuous_score` for a single-side format): the side's goals minus the other side's goals in regulation time (the shoot-out not counted); a side that forfeits gets -10.0.

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [RoboCup Humanoid Soccer League (HSL) Rule Book 2026, Laws 1-17 (its Laws of the Game follow the IFAB Laws of the Game)](https://github.com/RoboCup-HumanoidSoccerLeague/HSL-Rules) version 2026 (commit 06c44d4, 2026-06-29) |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | Law 1 | pitch 10 x 7 m (HSL S-Field 9 x 6, M-Field 14 x 9); boards 0.3 m high on the touchlines and goal lines (open goal mouths), no border strip; goals 2.6 x 1.8 m, 0.6 m deep |
| D2 | Law 3 | 2 v 2, no designated goalkeeper, no substitutes; robot-to-robot communication: in the team and team_match formats the team channel (at most 512 bytes per message, one message per robot every 0.2 game seconds, 4000 per robot and match, teammates only; 4000, not 3000: 3000 is exactly a full regular time of 600 s at the 0.2 s rate, so a robot that talks at the full rate would be refused in the shoot-out after it); in the match and duel formats one player commands both robots (no channel needed) |
| D3 | Laws 5-6 | an automatic, deterministic referee in the simulator instead of human referees and the GameController |
| D4 | Law 7 | 2 x 5 minutes of game time (HSL 2 x 10 min; 2 x 2.5 min up to soccer-2v2-4), a review at half time, no change of ends (each team's frame stays), no timeouts; the world and the clock freeze at every stoppage until the reviews; ball-stop extension at most 3 s; mercy rule (10 goals) kept |
| D5 | Law 8 | the referee places the robots for a kick-off (seeded positions, up to 0.3 m off the nominal spots); the ball is in play when it has moved 0.15 m or 10 s after play resumes; the kick-off team must touch the ball outside the centre circle before it can score (else no goal, the other team kicks off); dropped ball: ball on the centre mark, robots placed in their halves; game stuck: local 15 s (the nearest robot removed; 10 s up to soccer-2v2-3, longer now that a swing kick takes about 5 s), global 30 s (dropped ball), with a 0.3 m ball-movement threshold and 1 m proximity |
| D6 | Laws 9, 13, 15-17 | the boards keep the ball in: no kick-ins, goal kicks or corners; a ball resting at a board (within 0.3 m of a touchline, or of a goal line beside the goal, moved less than 0.3 m for 3 s) is moved 1 m straight inwards while play goes on; no free kicks (a foul only removes the offender); a ball that ever leaves the pitch restarts with a dropped ball |
| D7 | Law 10 | no draws: a level match goes straight to the penalty shoot-out |
| D8 | Law 12 (pushing) | measurable pushing: an opponent falls within 0.5 s of contact while the offender moved towards it faster (> 0.15 m/s more); or an opponent pushed more than 0.6 m back during one contact (gaps up to 0.5 s) by a robot moving towards it faster; or contact over 5 s (the faster mover); a kicking robot within 1.3 m of the ball is exempt |
| D9 | Law 12 (illegal position, defence) | added: both robots of a team inside their own penalty area (2 x 4 m, the goal included) for more than 5 s: the one farther from the ball is removed (not counted as an offence) |
| D10 | Law 12 (ball holding, fallen robot, removal penalty) | ball holding = the ball's centre within 0.16 m of a standing robot's trunk centre for more than 5 s; a fallen robot (trunk below 0.40 m) lies still 3 s and is stood up where it lies (no penalty: the walking policy cannot get up); removal penalty 15 s + 5 s per counted team offence (pushing, ball holding), served off the pitch beside the robot's own half, re-entry on the touchline; penalties end at half time; no cards |
| D11 | Law 14 | shoot-out: 3 kicks each, then up to 3 sudden-death rounds ranked by the HSL kick categories (goal, saved, post, wide, other, no kick), then a seeded coin toss; each team shoots at the goal it attacks; strikers robot 1, 2, 1, the keeper the other team's robot with the same number; 20 s to touch the ball; the keeper stays within 0.6 m of its line until the touch (else a goal); the team that kicked off first shoots first |
| D12 | Law 4 | same-colour team jerseys (A blue, B red) with bold white front and back numbers 1 and 2 |
| D13 | Law 4 (players: robots) | the robots are Booster T1 lower bodies (legs and trunk): the real T1's two 4-joint arms are not modelled (no arm motion, no arm contact, no dive or get-up motion); the legs are held to the real T1's limits (Booster URDF torques and joint speeds; estimates of bodies/booster_t1/body.toml: a linear torque-speed envelope, a rated torque of 60 % of the URDF torque with an I^2 t foldback after about 5 s at the peak, a 1 kW bus per robot, a walking-command rate limit) |
| D14 | Law 4 (players: robots), robot perception | each robot's own pose comes from the simulator (exact self-localization in the team frame); a real T1 localizes itself from its camera and odometry with errors of several centimetres to decimetres. The ball and the other robots are only in the camera images |
| D15 | Law 1 (field surface: artificial turf 20-30 mm) | the turf is a ball model calibrated to the FIFA Quality Programme for Football Turf (soccer-2v2-8; up to -7 the ball rolled with 0.15 m/s^2 and hardly bounced): a constant rolling deceleration of 0.52 m/s^2 (the FIFA roll test, a ball leaving a 1 m ramp at about 3.2 m/s, rolls 9.8 m here: allowed 4-10 m; the low end of 0.51-1.28 m/s^2, nearest RoboCup practice), a 2 m drop rebounds 0.81 m (allowed 0.60-1.00 m), the ball a thin shell (a ball struck at its centre skids and rolls on at 3/5 of its speed); not measured on a real HSL field (30 mm turf); a constant deceleration instead of one that grows with speed |
